title: Ajanta Pharma Recalls Schizophrenia Drug Fluphenazine 1 mg in US Over Impurity Failure

contentHtml:
Mumbai: Ajanta Pharma USA Inc. has recalled specific lots of Fluphenazine Hydrochloride Tablets, USP 1 mg in the United States after the product failed specifications for organic impurities during long-term stability testing. The recall has been classified as Class III.

The affected product is Fluphenazine Hydrochloride Tablets, USP, 1 mg, supplied in 100-count bottles as a prescription-only medicine. The product carries NDC 27241-255-01, is marketed by Ajanta Pharma USA Inc., Bridgewater, New Jersey, and is made in India.

The recall involves two lots, DJ23254, with an expiration date of November 30, 2026, and DJ10205, with an expiration date of April 30, 2027.

The reason for the recall is a failure of impurities/degradation specifications for Organic Impurities by HPLC (Impurity-A) during testing at the 18-month long-term stability interval. The reported test result was 1.1%, against a specification limit of 1.0%, resulting in an out-of-specification (OOS) finding.

Fluphenazine hydrochloride is an antipsychotic medicine belonging to the phenothiazine class. It is used for the management of psychotic disorders, including schizophrenia, and works primarily through effects on neurotransmitter activity in the central nervous system.

The medicine is available as an oral tablet and is a prescription-only product. Fluphenazine is used in the treatment of psychotic symptoms and may be prescribed as part of long-term management for patients with schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders.

The product carries the Ajanta Pharma USA Inc. marketing information and is manufactured in India. The recalling firm's US address is 400 Crossing Blvd, Suite 102, Bridgewater, New Jersey 08807-2863, United States.

Ajanta Pharma is a specialty pharmaceutical company with operations across international markets. Its business includes branded generics in India and emerging markets, generics in the United States and institutional business in Africa. The company has a research and development platform focused on pharmaceutical product development and differentiated formulations.

Ajanta Pharma has manufacturing facilities in India supporting the production of various pharmaceutical dosage forms and products supplied to domestic and regulated international markets. Its portfolio covers multiple therapeutic areas, while its US business focuses on generic pharmaceutical products.

The affected Fluphenazine Hydrochloride Tablets are specifically limited to the 1 mg strength in 100-count bottles carrying NDC 27241-255-01. The two affected lots are DJ23254 and DJ10205, with expiration dates of November 30, 2026, and April 30, 2027, respectively.

The quality issue identified in the affected batches relates specifically to Impurity-A detected through HPLC testing at the 18-month long-term stability interval. The impurity level was reported at 1.1% compared with the permitted specification of 1.0%.

The recall has been classified as Class III, which applies to situations where use of or exposure to the affected product is not likely to cause adverse health consequences. The action concerns the identified lots of Ajanta Pharma's fluphenazine tablets and does not indicate a recall of all fluphenazine products.
